issues.description: raise PerformanceWarning(msg) raises a Warning subclass as an exception — warn-vs-error contract is undecided
issues.detail: The code does `raise PerformanceWarning(msg)`, but PerformanceWarning is a Warning subclass that by convention should be emitted via `warnings.warn`. The test asserts via `pytest.raises`, the test name says `_warns`, and the PR description openly asks 'Would an exception be appropriate here?'. This conflates two distinct concerns — advisory ('program may proceed') vs fatal ('program cannot proceed'). Decide the policy: either `warnings.warn(msg, PerformanceWarning)` and continue, or raise a real exception class (e.g., ValueError or a dedicated subclass), then align the class name, the test name, and the assertion.

issues.description: Unreachable `break` after `raise` — dead code reveals confused control flow
issues.detail: Inside the per-axis loop, `raise PerformanceWarning(msg)` is immediately followed by `break`. The break is unreachable. This betrays an unstated loop invariant: is the contract 'fail on the first misaligned axis' (then no break needed) or 'collect all misalignments and report once' (then don't raise inside the loop)? State the invariant and remove the dead statement.

issues.description: SPEC-MISSING: contract of to_zarr under shard/config conflict is undefined
issues.detail: The PR author explicitly asks in the description what should happen when the global `array.chunk-size` config competes with the zarr shard shape, and the code ships one policy (raise) without that question resolved. There are at least three coherent policies: (a) global config wins with a warning, (b) shard shape wins silently or with a warning, (c) conflict is a hard ValueError. Choose one, document it on `to_zarr`'s docstring (preconditions/postconditions), and align the implementation, the exception/warning class name, and tests to it.

issues.description: safe_chunk_size formula is dimensionally incoherent and uses suspicious `max(1, itemsize)` guard
issues.detail: Inside the per-axis loop checking divisibility on axis `ax`, `safe_chunk_size = np.prod(zarr_write_chunks) * max(1, z.dtype.itemsize)` computes the byte size of one whole shard — a global quantity used to diagnose a per-axis violation. Either the postcondition is `array.chunk-size >= one full shard in bytes` (in which case the loop should not be per-axis) or it is per-axis (in which case the formula is wrong). The `max(1, itemsize)` guards against a case (zero-itemsize dtype) zarr already excludes; silently lying about size is worse than failing. Also, `np.prod` on a tuple may produce a numpy scalar that f-string-embeds awkwardly — cast to int. State the postcondition, then write the formula.

issues.description: Error message advises setting `array.chunk-size` to a raw byte int, but the config expects a units-parsed string
issues.detail: The error message tells the user to call `dask.config.set({'array.chunk-size': N})` with a raw integer, but dask's `array.chunk-size` is conventionally a units-parsed string like '128MiB' (via parse_bytes). The suggested snippet may technically work but is not how anyone configures it, and a user later seeing `array.chunk-size: 7200` in config will not remember it's bytes. Lead with the cause ('Your dask config array.chunk-size of X is smaller than the Zarr shard size of Y bytes'), then show the remedy in human-readable form (e.g., `format_bytes(safe_chunk_size)`).

issues.description: Divisibility check uses only `dw[0]` per axis, silently assuming uniform chunks
issues.detail: `nominal_dask_chunk_size = dw[0]` inspects only the first chunk on each axis. `normalize_chunks` does not promise uniform tuples — it returns a tuple precisely because chunks may vary. The check `forall axes: dw[0] % zw == 0` is not the property the safety argument requires. State the invariant explicitly ('every interior block is a multiple of the shard size; the trailing remainder is allowed'), and assert `all(c % zw == 0 for c in dw[:-1])` or document why `dw[0]` suffices for this code path.

issues.description: Test asserts pytest.raises on a class named *Warning* while the test name says 'warns' — codifies the wrong contract
issues.detail: `test_zarr_risky_shards_warns` uses `pytest.raises(PerformanceWarning, ...)`. Three signals disagree: the test name (warns), the class name (Warning), and the assertion (raises). Once the warn-vs-raise contract is decided, align all three: either rename to `_raises` and use a dedicated exception, or switch to `pytest.warns` plus `warnings.warn` in the implementation.

issues.description: Validation logic is complected with to_zarr — should be a single pure filter function
issues.detail: The added block does three intertwined things inside to_zarr: (1) computes candidate dask chunking via normalize_chunks, (2) walks axes checking shard-alignment, (3) constructs a user-facing error message with a recommended config value. None of these are about writing to zarr. Lift into `_align_dask_chunks_to_shards(dask_chunks, zarr_write_chunks, dtype) -> (aligned_chunks, Optional[diagnostic])` returning data rather than raising. Then to_zarr decides whether that data becomes a warning, an error, or a silent re-plan. The data flow and test surface both shrink.

issues.description: Region branch may not be covered by the alignment audit it claims to enforce
issues.detail: The per-axis alignment audit runs before the `if region is None` split, but in the region branch the rechunk is rebuilt per axis via `new_blockdim(s, c, r)`, which can differ from `dask_write_chunks`. So the property the warning is supposed to guarantee — that the chunks actually written to the store are shard-aligned — is checked against a different chunking than the one that will be written. State the postcondition (writes are shard-aligned) and verify it on the chunking that will be written.

issues.description: Patch bundles two changes — refactor the region/no-region branches AND add the alignment check
issues.detail: The diff hoists `dask_write_chunks` out of both branches (a clean refactor: the duplicated `_get_zarr_write_chunks` + `normalize_chunks` was ugly) AND introduces the new alignment error path. These are two patches. The hoist should land independently because it's an unambiguous win; the warn-vs-error behavior is what's actually under debate. Splitting would let the cleanup land while the contract question gets resolved.

Use `nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw != 0`. The `not X % Y == 0` form parses correctly via operator precedence but forces the reader to consult the precedence table. The simpler version is one token shorter and unambiguous.

`normalize_chunks` never returns an empty tuple for any axis with shape > 0, so the guard either protects nothing or protects a degenerate case the rest of the function doesn't handle. Drop it or replace with an explicit precondition.

The PR description explains the key insight — `auto_chunks` 'nearly always concatenates the previous_chunks argument', so passing the shard shape yields shard-multiple chunks. This insight belongs in a comment above the `normalize_chunks` call. A reader six months from now will see `previous_chunks=zarr_write_chunks` and wonder why the *shard* shape is being labeled 'previous'. One sentence resolves it.

issues.description: Variable naming thicket: zarr_write_chunks vs dask_write_chunks vs zarr_chunk_shape vs zarr_shard_shape
issues.detail: Within ~30 lines the code carries `zarr_write_chunks`, `dask_write_chunks`, `nominal_dask_chunk_size`, and `zw`/`dw`. The test file adds `zarr_chunk_shape` and `zarr_shard_shape`. Reader has to juggle four near-synonyms. Consider `target_chunks` and `shard_chunks`; short loop variables are fine if the outer names are unambiguous. Also clarify in the message whether the on-disk granularity is 'chunk' or 'shard' for the given array, instead of 'chunk (or shard)'.

issues.description: Test asserts only `chunksize` (first block), under-stating the alignment property
issues.detail: `assert all(c % s == 0 for c, s in zip(result.chunksize, zarr_shard_shape))` only checks the nominal block size on each axis. Assert the full property: for every axis, every block except possibly the last is a multiple of the shard size, and the last block is `<=` shard size or aligned to the array edge. That is the invariant the production code is supposed to guarantee.

issues.description: Test imports PerformanceWarning from dask.array.core — boundary not stated
issues.detail: If `PerformanceWarning` is intended as public API, it should be exported via `__all__` and documented; if internal, the test reaches across the module boundary. Draw the boundary — promote to public contract or use the resolved exception/warning class so the test doesn't pin an internal name.

synthesis.summary: The mechanical idea — pass the zarr shard shape as `previous_chunks` to `normalize_chunks` so `auto_chunks` grows shard-aligned chunks — is sound and a clear improvement to `to_zarr`'s contract. But the safety check bolted on top of it ships an undecided design: the code does `raise PerformanceWarning(msg)` (a Warning subclass raised as an exception), followed by an unreachable `break`, with a test named `_warns` that uses `pytest.raises` — and the PR description itself openly asks whether this should be a warning or an exception. Resolve that contract first, then align the class name, the test name, and the assertion. Additional issues: `safe_chunk_size = np.prod(shard) * max(1, itemsize)` is dimensionally incoherent for a per-axis diagnostic and recommends a raw int for a units-parsed config key; the divisibility check inspects only `dw[0]` per axis without stating the uniformity invariant; the region branch may bypass the audit it claims to enforce; and the alignment logic should be lifted to a pure filter function. The hoist of `dask_write_chunks` out of both branches is a clean refactor that could land independently while the warn-vs-raise policy is decided.
